_note: Every non-Lighthouse figure in the Health Check report. Security and maintenance tables, their ratios and counts are generated from these checks; every other number in the report text must equal a value here, in data.json (Lighthouse) or in offer.json, or the build fails (scripts/health-check.mjs).

security.evidence: The only administrator is "admin" with a weak password; "admin" is the first name every automated attack tries.
security.fix: Create a new administrator with a non-obvious name and a long passphrase, demote and remove "admin".

security.evidence: No limit on failed sign-in attempts and no second factor.
security.fix: One lightweight login-protection plugin; two-factor for both partners and the assistant.

security.evidence: Page source advertises "WordPress {{audit.facts.wp_version}}" and "Elementor {{audit.facts.elementor_version}}" and appends version numbers to asset URLs.
security.fix: Remove the generator tags and version query strings (a few lines in the child theme).

security.evidence: No backup plugin or host backup is configured. A bad update or a compromise means a rebuild.
security.fix: Daily automatic backup to off-site storage, {{audit.facts.backup_retention_days}}-day retention, one restore tested and documented.

security.evidence: Three plugins (Elementor, Fluent Forms, Yoast SEO), all current, none abandoned or duplicated.
security.fix: Keep as is; add a monthly update routine (see Maintenance).

security.evidence: Submit requests carry a one-time token (confirmed). The plugin's honeypot and submission limit are available but off, so bots can flood the intake form.
security.fix: Turn on the honeypot and a per-address submission limit (dashboard settings, no code).

security.evidence: Both are on by default in WordPress; the live server's setting could not be confirmed from the copy reviewed.
security.fix: Disable XML-RPC unless the firm uses the mobile app; block the users endpoint for anonymous requests.

security.check: HTTPS, security headers, file editing in dashboard
security.evidence: Needs the live host; checked in the first hour of any fix engagement.
security.fix: Force HTTPS, add standard headers, set DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT.

maintenance.evidence: {{audit.facts.wp_version}}, the current release at review time.
Hello Elementor child theme, Elementor {{audit.facts.elementor_version}}, Fluent Forms {{audit.facts.fluentforms_version}}, Yoast SEO {{audit.facts.yoast_version}}.

maintenance.check: Update routine with a staging copy
maintenance.evidence: Updates are applied (or not) by hand on the live site. No staging copy exists to test an update before visitors see it.
See Security. Counted here as well because it is the maintenance safety net.
Nothing alerts the firm if the site goes down or the intake form stops sending.
Hosting, domain and admin logins are known to one person. A short access sheet in the firm's password manager removes that single point of failure.
